comparator.name: Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official curriculum totals 180 ECTS. Years 1 and 2 each contain 60 ECTS of microeconomics, macroeconomics, quantitative methods, programming, finance and applied economic analysis. Year 3 comprises a 30-ECTS mobility/minor/internship window, 12 ECTS of electives chosen from the published list, a 6-ECTS philosophy-and-history course and a 12-ECTS thesis. Zero-credit GROW activity is excluded; genuine choice space is not filled with assumed courses.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces experimental methods, marketing, consumer-product work, organisational psychology and market research with programming, database systems, computational decision-making, linear algebra and advanced calculus. It differs still more clearly from the behavioural route, which concentrates on psychology, marketing, persuasion and consumer response.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest curriculum covers the programme-wide microeconomic, macroeconomic and quantitative core. Public economics/institutions/inequality and financial economics each support coherent, mechanically feasible and substantially distinct UCR alternatives. Behavioral and experimental economics is a further evidenced direction, but no fourth alternative can be included.

notes.text: Tilburg requires a sustained economics sequence spanning welfare, international finance, game theory, industrial economics, growth, development, communication with data and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can build coherent economics pathways, but it does not reproduce that full specialist sequence.
